annotations.title: Classify one AI system against the routes of the Regulation

description: Use this as the first step when you hold a concrete AI system and need to know which routes of the EU AI Act come into view: prohibited practice screening, Annex III high risk, transparency, FRIA and the general purpose model route, and with a version 2 profile the wider set of duties, such as Article 26 for a deployer. It runs the deterministic decision engine over coded answers and returns one applicability status per assessed obligation, with the timing and what is still open. It is not meant for a general question about the law. An obligation the engine did not assess is listed in assessment_scope.not_assessed with the reason; it was not found inapplicable. It does not return a single coded classification label.

detail.description: Amount of data to return. brief keeps the outcome, the dates, the reasons, the open questions and the source with its locator; full adds the complete objects, every statement text and every hash, for re-computation or archiving.

lang.description: Language of the labels and explanations. Dutch is the default.

profile.description: The coded answers about one system. The fifteen version 1 fields are required. A field that does not bear on this case takes not_relevant, and unsure is a real answer that leads to insufficient_context rather than to a guess. A version 1 profile has five obligations assessed. To have the wider set assessed, including Article 26 for a deployer of a high risk system, also send profile_version 2.0.0, chain_roles (consistent with actor_role) and the twelve other version 2 scope facts: ai_system_scope, jurisdiction_established_in_eu, jurisdiction_market_in_eu, jurisdiction_output_in_eu, scope_exclusion, annex_i_product, annex_i_third_party_conformity, article_25_role_change, provider_outside_eu, sandbox_participation, real_world_testing and adverse_significant_decision. The remaining version 2 facts are optional: an unanswered fact is unknown and leads to insufficient_context, never to a silent no. The backend rejects a profile whose answers contradict each other.

actor_role.description: The role the assessed organisation occupies for this system.

adverse_significant_decision.description: Version 2: can the output lead to a decision with legal or similarly significant adverse effects on a person (Article 86)?

ai_system_scope.description: Version 2: is the assessed thing an AI system in the sense of Article 3(1)?

annex_i_product.description: Version 2: is the system a product, or a safety component of a product, under the Union legislation in Annex I?

annex_i_third_party_conformity.description: Version 2: does that product need a third party conformity assessment? not_relevant without an Annex I product.

annex_iii_domain.description: The Annex III domain of the intended purpose.

annex_iii_use_case.description: The coded Annex III use case. Its prefix must match the domain: employment takes emp-, education takes edu-, and so on. none with domain none, unsure with domain unsure.

article_25_already_high_risk.description: Version 2, optional: with a role change, is the system concerned already high risk? not_relevant without a role change.

article_25_role_change.description: Version 2: a role change under Article 25(1), or none.

article_50_market_date.description: Required for a provider with the synthetic_content scenario, not_relevant otherwise.

article_50_scenarios.description: The transparency scenarios of Article 50 that occur. none and unsure are exclusive: neither combines with another value.

article_5_signal.description: Screening signal for the prohibited practices of Article 5.

article_6_3_documented.description: Version 2, optional: is the Article 6(3) assessment documented?

article_6_3_exception.description: Version 2, optional: which condition of Article 6(3) is invoked, if any.

article_6_3_no_significant_risk.description: Version 2, optional: is there no significant risk of harm in the sense of Article 6(3)?

article_6_3_profiling.description: Version 2, optional: does the system perform profiling of natural persons?

chain_roles.description: Version 2: the roles in the value chain, kept apart. Must agree with actor_role, for example [deployer] with actor_role deployer.

complaint_to_authority.description: Version 2, optional: has a complaint been lodged with a market surveillance authority?

controlled_input_data.description: Version 2, optional: does the deployer exercise control over the input data (Article 26(4))?

decision_influence.description: Required when an exact Annex III use case is named, not_relevant otherwise.

decisions_about_people.description: Version 2, optional: does the system make or assist decisions about natural persons (Article 26(11))?

direct_interaction_obvious.description: Required with the direct_interaction scenario, not_relevant otherwise.

eu_nexus.description: The connection to the Union market. none leads to out of scope.

fria_context.description: Required for a deployer with an exact Annex III use case other than ci-2, not_relevant otherwise.

gpai_commission_designated.description: Version 2, optional: has the Commission designated the model as having systemic risk?

gpai_compute_above_threshold.description: Version 2, optional: is the training compute above the threshold of Article 51(2)?

gpai_high_impact_capabilities.description: Version 2, optional: does the model have high impact capabilities under Article 51(1)(a)?

gpai_market_date.description: Required when the model is placed on the Union market, not_relevant otherwise.

gpai_open_source_status.description: Required when the model is placed on the Union market, not_relevant otherwise.

gpai_systemic_notification.description: Version 2, optional: has the Commission been notified under Article 52(1)?

gpai_union_market.description: Required for a general purpose model provider, not_relevant otherwise.

jurisdiction_established_in_eu.description: Version 2: is the organisation established in the Union?

jurisdiction_market_in_eu.description: Version 2: is the system placed on the market or put into service in the Union?

jurisdiction_output_in_eu.description: Version 2: is the output used in the Union?

law_enforcement_remote_identification.description: Version 2, optional: is the system used for post remote biometric identification in law enforcement (Article 26(10))?

logs_under_control.description: Version 2, optional: are the automatically generated logs under the control of the deployer (Article 26(6))?

object_type.description: What is being assessed: a system, a general purpose model, or a system built on one.

personal_data_processing.description: Version 2, optional: does the use involve processing of personal data (Article 26(9))?

profile_version.description: Send 2.0.0 to have the wider set of obligations assessed. Omit it for a version 1 profile.

provider_outside_eu.description: Version 2: is the provider established outside the Union?

public_authority_deployer.description: Version 2, optional: is the deployer a public authority or Union body (Article 26(8))?

public_interest_editorial_control.description: Required for a deployer with the public_interest_text scenario, not_relevant otherwise.

real_world_testing.description: Version 2: is the system tested in real world conditions outside a sandbox?

risk_detected.description: Version 2, optional: has a risk in the sense of Article 79(1) been detected?

safety_component.description: Version 2, optional: is the system used as a safety component?

sandbox_participation.description: Version 2: does the system take part in an AI regulatory sandbox?

scope_exclusion.description: Version 2: an exclusion under Article 2, or none.

serious_incident.description: Version 2, optional: has a serious incident occurred?

third_party_components_integrated.description: Version 2, optional: does a third party supply components that are integrated in the system?

workplace_use.description: Version 2, optional: is the system put into service or used at the workplace (Article 26(7))?

name: classify_system

assessment_scope.description: What this assessment did and did not assess, from the engine itself. not_assessed groups the obligations that were not assessed by reason (for example profile_version_below_2), with the facts that would have them assessed. Not assessed is not the same as not applying.

high_risk_regime_from.description: Practical date next to a text date.

provenance.description: Which published endpoints produced this result. Every call is listed with its full URL, so a reader can re-issue it and check the answer rather than trust it.

title: Classify one AI system against the routes of the Regulation
